notes:
Stage/context:
- Procurement-stage POC for real-time routing assistant; wanted sub-100ms 95th pct for short prompts.
- Heavy burst traffic windows during morning dispatch and EOD — spikes ~5-7x baseline.
- Primary technical concern: queueing under burst + KV cache reuse for many short-lived chat sessions.
AE/SE synopsis:
- Avery Chen (AE): introduced Redwood Dedicated and Dedicated+Autoscale options. SE demo'd batching profiles.
- Samir Patel (SE): ran throughput projection for their 60k daily requests; recommended 2 dedicated pools with burst policy. Provided cost-vs-latency tradeoffs.
Customer feedback (paraphrase):
- "We need guaranteed throughput during morning spikes — can't tolerate >200ms tail latencies or queuing that drops requests."
- Security team liked VPC + KMS but insisted on prescriptive throughput SLA and transparent queueing model.
POC notes / results:
- Short POC (2 weeks): Redwood Dedicated meeting latency SLO on baseline, but under synthetic 6x burst we saw queueing and preemption impacts on lower-priority pools.
- Customer ran a competing vendor (Cohere-managed endpoints) side-by-side; competitor demoed auto-sharding + seamless burst scaling in their cloud demo and promised 99.9% burst-capacity SLA.
Decision/outcome:
- Technical fit borderline: PeakFlow could accept Redwood if we provided clear automatic burst-scaling path and a documented queueing/fallback policy mapping to their SLAs.
- Business outcome: budget freeze + engineering lead (internal champion) left on 02/01; procurement deprioritized. Customer elected to go with competitor proof that promised autoscale, citing lower risk during peak windows.
Next actions (internal):
- Mark as closed-lost.
- Add to OEM re-engage list for Q4 when budget cycle resets.
- Share POC logs and synthetic burst test results with Product (INF-1987) — request clearer autoscale patterns and an official burst-capacity playbook.
Misc snippets:
- Security review link shared: drive://security/peakflow-security-reqs.docx
- Quote from IT director: "We can't gamble on opaque queueing during our peak 30-minute dispatch window."
- Follow-up cadence attempted: 3x emails, 2 calls, 1 security deep-dive (no response after 02/20).
